tasks.intent: Stop active application and agent work without leaking ownership or publishing a second outcome.
tasks.acceptance: The agent identifies the stop boundary and produces a compile-and-test-correct change using only documented controls.

tasks.intent: Create a complete package from a fixed behavioral brief.
tasks.acceptance: The package compiles, its tests pass, and all external operations and authority requirements are explicit.

tasks.intent: Diagnose and repair a seeded type, ownership, effect, or runtime failure.
tasks.acceptance: The repair passes the fixed regression and does not weaken authority, recovery, or resource limits.

tasks.intent: Explain the behavior and authority boundaries of a complete representative program.
tasks.acceptance: The explanation locates every external operation, suspension point, ownership transfer, and release boundary.

tasks.intent: Modify a representative program while preserving its fixed behavioral contract.
tasks.acceptance: The modified package compiles and passes old and new tests without ambient authority or fixture substitution.

tasks.intent: Review a representative program for authority, protected release, recovery, and shutdown defects.
tasks.acceptance: No critical authority or release boundary is missed and every reported defect cites a source-visible boundary.

tasks.intent: Operate the long-running service through repeated bounded work and orderly shutdown.
tasks.acceptance: The service remains bounded by declared quotas and settles all owned work during shutdown.

applications.intent: Compose typed errors, artifacts, capabilities, live I/O, concurrency, source tools, protected release, and lifecycle.
Exercise DNS, TLS, streaming I/O, cancellation, cleanup, and bounded concurrency.
Reuse the portable agent library while proving transcript, tool-result, and resume recovery without live resources.
Exercise explicit filesystem, environment, console, typed-error, and cleanup capabilities.
Exercise listeners, streaming HTTP, mutable single-owner state, quotas, stop, and shutdown.
Exercise pure packages, collections, iterators, closures, parsing, and typed errors.
Exercise confined process launch, pipes, concurrent drain, cancellation, and reaping.
